questions.q: WannaCry, the global outbreak of May 2017 that encrypted systems and demanded bitcoin payments, was:
questions.solution: WannaCry was ransomware - it encrypted victims' files and demanded ransom (in bitcoin), spreading via the EternalBlue exploit against unpatched Windows.
questions.shortcut: Encrypt + demand money = ransomware; WannaCry is the stock example.

questions.q: The Rehearse Timings feature is used to:
options: Record the time spent on each slide for automatic advance
Time the download of the file
questions.solution: Rehearse Timings records how long each slide stays on screen while you practise, then can auto-advance the show using those durations - essential for self-running kiosks.
questions.shortcut: Practise now, auto-advance later - that is Rehearse Timings.

questions.q: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by:
questions.solution: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN in 1989 and wrote the first browser. Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP; Larry Page co-founded Google.
questions.shortcut: Web = Berners-Lee, 1989, CERN. Internet (1970s TCP/IP) = Cerf and Kahn.

questions.q: Assembly language mnemonics such as ADD and MOV are converted into machine code by a(n):
questions.solution: An assembler translates assembly (2GL) mnemonics into machine language. Compilers/interpreters work on high-level (3GL) languages; preprocessors transform source text before compilation.
questions.shortcut: Assembly -> Assembler (same first letters); high-level -> compiler/interpreter.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He asked me if I was hungry.
options: He said to me, "Are you hungry?"
He said to me, "You are hungry."
He said to me, "Was I hungry?"
He said to me, "Are I hungry?"
questions.solution: 'asked if' = yes/no question → restore quotes, question order and **present tense** (was → are), you as listener. B states instead of asking; C reverses the pronouns; D writes the impossible 'Are I'.
questions.shortcut: Reverse: if + was → Are you …? with question mark.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: When *every* repeats before both nouns, the subject stays singular: every man and every woman **was counted**. The pair feeling in part 1 tempts the plural, but the rule holds.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

After the inquiry, the rumour ___ to be completely false.
questions.solution: The sense is 'proved to be': **turned out** to be false. 'Turned up' means appeared, 'turned down' means rejected, 'turned over' means handed over or flipped.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: The control room answers complaints round the clock **during** the monsoon — right through that period. *Within* needs a length ('within a month'), *since* needs a starting point with a perfect tense, and *among* takes a plural group, not a season.
questions.shortcut: Period through which something continues → during.
questions.passage: Every June the municipal office on the fourth floor turns into a monsoon war room. The control room answers complaints round the clock (1) ______ the monsoon, and staff keep sandbags ready for the low-lying ward. The executive engineer insists that drains must be desilted (2) ______ the first showers arrive, not after them. Contractors who delay the work are fined (3) ______ of repeated warnings. Residents can now report a blocked drain by phone, and the office responds (4) ______ every complaint within a day.

questions.q: The boundary between the Earth's crust and the mantle is called the:
questions.solution: The **Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity** separates the crust from the mantle. Gutenberg separates mantle and core, Lehmann separates outer and inner core, and Conrad lies within the crust.
questions.shortcut: 'Come Make Good Lunch' — Moho is second.

questions.q: The **Shaka era**, used for India's national calendar, was started in 78 CE by —
questions.solution: The Shaka Samvat (78 CE) is traditionally credited to the Kushana king **Kanishka**. It was adopted as the base of India's **National Calendar** (from 22 March 1957). Vikram Samvat starts in 57 BCE.

questions.q: Evidence of a **ploughed field** belonging to the Harappan period has been discovered at —
questions.solution:
**Kalibangan** (Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar) shows a ploughed field with criss-cross furrows, plus fire altars. The name means 'black bangles'.

Trap: Banawali (Haryana) has a **clay model** of a plough, not a field.

questions.q: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees:
options: 100 days of employment per household, as under MGNREGA
125 days of wage employment per rural household per year, effective 1 July 2026
questions.solution: The VB-G RAM G Act (2025) raises the statutory guarantee from 100 to **125 days** per rural household per financial year and came into force on **1 July 2026**, with weekly wage payments replacing the 15-day cycle.

questions.q: From the roof of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is $60^\circ$ and the angle of depression of its base is $45^\circ$. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution:
Depression $45^\circ$: horizontal distance $d=\frac{7}{\tan45^\circ}=7$ m.

Elevation $60^\circ$: top above roof $=7\tan60^\circ=7\sqrt3$.

Tower $=7+7\sqrt3=7(1+\sqrt3)$ m.
questions.shortcut: 45° depression gives $d$ = building height (7); tower $=7+7\sqrt3$. Add the building back — the top angle only measures the part above the roof.

questions.q: Find the least number which when divided by 6, 9 and 12 leaves remainders 5, 8 and 11 respectively.
questions.solution:
Each remainder is 1 less than its divisor → N + 1 is divisible by 6, 9 and 12.
LCM $= 36$ → N $= 36 - 1 = 35$.
Check: $35 = 5 \times 6 + 5 = 3 \times 9 + 8 = 2 \times 12 + 11$ ✓.

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle $ABC$, $AB=AC=25$ cm and $BC=14$ cm. The area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
The median/altitude to the base: $h=\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=24$ cm.

Area $=\frac12\times14\times24=168\ \text{cm}^2$.
questions.shortcut: 7-24-25 again: height 24, area $=\frac12\times14\times24=168$. Trap: 336 forgot the $\frac12$.

questions.q: In a pie chart of family expenditure, rent takes 22% of the total. The central angle of the rent sector is:
questions.solution: $22\times3.6^\circ=79.2^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: Percent to angle: multiply by 3.6. $22\times3.6=79.2^\circ$. Trap: $72^\circ$ (used 3° per percent... or mixed up with 20%).

questions.q:
**Statement:** The municipal corporation has decided to plant 10,000 trees along city roads to reduce air pollution.

**Assumptions:**
I. After the trees are planted, the city will become completely free of air pollution.
II. Trees can help reduce air pollution to some extent.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution: I expects a total result; the corporation only needs some reduction to make the plan worthwhile — **not implicit**. Negate II: trees do nothing for pollution — the decision is pointless, so II is **implicit**. Answer: **only II**.
questions.shortcut: 'Completely' = total effect = not implicit. 'To some extent' = implicit.

questions.q: **A man is facing West. He turns 90° anticlockwise, then 270° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?**
questions.solution: Quarters: anticlockwise 90° = −1, clockwise 270° = +3. Net = +2 quarter turns. W + 2 (on the cycle W → N → E) = **East**.
questions.shortcut: Add turns as quarter turns (right +, left −) before touching the compass.

questions.q:
Select the letter that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**Z, W, T, Q, N, ?**

**Statements:** Some flowers are red. No flower is blue.

**Conclusions:** I. All flowers are red. II. Some flowers are not red.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: The red part of flowers isn't fixed as all or some-not, so neither conclusion is provable — but they are exact negations, so one of them must hold. **Either-or.**
questions.shortcut: (All, Some-not) pair on the same terms = complementary.
